stem: A client taking doxycycline asks why the nurse recommended limiting direct sunlight and using protective measures outdoors. Which response is most accurate?

options.A: Doxycycline can cause photosensitivity with an exaggerated sunburn reaction.
options.B: Doxycycline predictably causes permanent skin discoloration in every client exposed to sunlight.
options.C: Sunlight prevents doxycycline absorption, so exposure makes each dose ineffective.
options.D: The advice is only for comfort because doxycycline has no clinically important skin or light-related adverse effects.

rationale: A is correct. Current DailyMed labeling warns that tetracyclines, including doxycycline, can cause photosensitivity manifested by an exaggerated sunburn reaction and advises limiting sun exposure. B overstates tissue hyperpigmentation as universal and sun-dependent. C is not a labeled mechanism. D contradicts the photosensitivity warning.
educational_objective: Teach clients taking doxycycline that photosensitivity may cause exaggerated sunburn and that direct sunlight or ultraviolet exposure should be limited according to the product warning.
source_organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling via DailyMed
source_document_title: Doxycycline Hyclate Delayed-Release Tablets Prescribing Information
source_locator: Warnings and Precautions, Section 5.3 Photosensitivity: photosensitivity manifested by an exaggerated sunburn reaction has been observed with tetracyclines; limit sun exposure. Adverse Reactions also lists photosensitivity.
source_claim_supported: Doxycycline can cause photosensitivity with exaggerated sunburn reactions and patients should limit sun exposure.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: provide medication education and recognize adverse effects and precautions.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the item around the exact current DailyMed warning and removed universal or cosmetic claims not supported by the label.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A matches the label; B-D do not.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; photosensitivity is a labeled warning.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices address the same teaching issue.
audit_findings.blueprint: Medication adverse-effect teaching fits Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked hyperpigmentation versus photosensitivity and ensured the answer does not imply every client will react. PASS.
